body: Credit Suisse's share price was ~CHF 70+ in 2007 and ~CHF 0.76 equivalent in the UBS rescue on 19 Mar 2023 (UBS paid CHF 3 bn in stock; ~CHF 16 bn of AT1 bonds written to zero while shareholders got something -- inverting the usual hierarchy). Path: Mozambique 'tuna bonds' (2013-16), spying scandal (2019), Greensill supply-chain funds ($10 bn frozen, Mar 2021), Archegos loss ($5.5 bn, Mar-Apr 2021), repeated CEO/chair changes, a 2022 strategic overhaul and CHF 4 bn rights issue; Q4 2022 client outflows of ~CHF 110 bn; 14 Mar 2023 annual report disclosed 'material weaknesses' in controls (PwC); 15 Mar Saudi National Bank (top holder) said it would 'absolutely not' add capital; SNB liquidity line failed to stop the run. Visible flags: (1) CDS spreads blowing out in Oct 2022; (2) serial risk-management failures = culture, not bad luck; (3) price-to-tangible-book ~0.2-0.3 'cheapness' for years; (4) management turnover; (5) wealth-management outflows; (6) auditor material-weakness opinion. Lesson: a bank trading far below book for years with repeated scandals is a value trap -- the discount is the market pricing hidden losses and run risk. AT1s are equity-like in a crisis.

data.early_signals: serial scandals; CDS spike Oct 2022; outflows; material weakness; P/TBV ~0.2
data.lesson: Persistent deep discount + scandals = value trap

title: Credit Suisse (Mar 2023): death by a thousand scandals
